channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: United States Dollar Index climbs as Middle East tensions, Fed rate hike bets lift demand
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) consolidates modest gains on Wednesday as traders assess renewed tensions between the United States and Iran and the potential economic fallout.

item.title: Fed Minutes to reveal more about the Warsh era
item.description: The United States (US) Federal Reserve (Fed) will release the Minutes of the June 16-17 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Wednesday at 18:00 GMT. The Minutes should shed more light on the Fed’s hawkish hold delivered at Kevin Warsh’s first meeting as Fed Chair.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Oil shock weighs JPY against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret highlight renewed weakness in the Japanese Yen (JPY), which is underperforming G10 peers and threatening fresh multi-decade lows as USD/JPY trades at levels last seen in 1986.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: RBNZ hike underpins kiwi – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole reports that the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) raised rates to 2.50%, delivering a more hawkish message than expected and signalling further tightening is likely.

item.title: Australian Dollar remains pressured amid Trump comments
item.description: AUD/USD trades under pressure near 0.6920 on Wednesday, even after the US Dollar (USD) held firm amid geopolitical risk and caution ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) Minutes.

item.title: United Kingdom: Market watching Burnham – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses UK political dynamics, noting Burnham’s likely unchallenged path to becoming Prime Minister on July 20 and his popularity within Labour.

item.title: British Pound: Recovery eyes 1.36 against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the British Pound (GBP) is slightly softer but supported by a sharp repricing of Bank of England (BoE) tightening.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Hawkish Fed minutes may support greenback – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes that recent equity jitters and firm Oil prices have underlined the Dollar’s safe-haven appeal, while markets look to the June Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes.

item.title: Gold slides as renewed US-Iran tensions revive Fed rate hike bets, FOMC Minutes loom
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) sees a sharp move lower on Wednesday after US President Donald Trump declared that the ceasefire deal with Iran was “over” during the NATO Summit in Ankara, Turkey. However, Reuters later reported that Trump did not repeat those remarks, citing a source familiar with the talks.

item.title: India: Gradual firming CPI supports RBI patience – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategist Kunal Kundu expects India’s June 2026 headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation to print around 4.1% year-on-year, slightly above May’s 3.9% but still within the RBI’s tolerance band.

item.title: Silver falls as Trump renews Iran threats, boosts US Dollar ahead of Fed Minutes
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) extends its decline on Wednesday and trades around $58.45 at the time of writing. The white metal remains under pressure after comments from US President Donald Trump revived concerns about renewed conflict in the Middle East, supporting the US Dollar (USD) and US Treasury yields.

item.title: Euro steadies above 1.1400 as traders assess US-Iran tensions
item.description: EUR/USD treads water above the 1.1400 mark on Wednesday, steadying after coming under selling pressure as traders assess renewed US-Iran tensions after both sides exchanged fire overnight following attacks on commercial ships near the Strait of Hormuz earlier this week.

item.title: Mexican Peso: High real yields underpin MXN demand – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategists Christian Lawrence and Molly Schwartz note that despite Moody’s downgrade of Mexico to Baa3, 10-year MBono yields have fallen and markets remain relaxed about Mexico’s investment-grade status.

item.title: Euro: Geopolitics and ECB repricing supports EUR – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the Euro (EUR) is consolidating around the low 1.14s, with mixed G10 performance as markets reassess Oil’s impact on Euro area terms of trade and the European Central Bank’s (ECB) rate path.

item.title: United Kingdom: Early election scenarios – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered analysis by Christopher Graham and Saabir Salad discusses Andy Burnham’s stance against an early UK general election if he becomes prime minister.

item.title: Donald Trump says US may hit Iran again tonight, doubts deal holds
item.description: United States (US) President Donald Trump stepped up his rhetoric against Iran on Wednesday on the sidelines of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) summit, according to comments cited by Reuters.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: RBNZ hikes but warns of more – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu reports that the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) raised its Official Cash Rate (OCR) by 25bp to 2.50% to steer inflation back to 2%. The committee still sees further removal of stimulus as likely, though data will guide decisions.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Rebound meets strong USD resistance – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note that the Canadian Dollar (CAD) has held up well through recent Iran-driven volatility, extending its rebound even as the US Dollar (USD) trades mixed.

item.title: United States: Inflation expectations edge higher as oil rises – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research’s Philip Wee reports that the New York Fed’s June Survey of Consumer Expectations showed 1-year inflation expectations rising to 3.7%, with 3-year expectations at 3.3% and 5-year unchanged at 3%.

item.title: Canada: Trade surplus at four-year high – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada’s (NBC) strategist Alexandra Ducharme reports Canada’s merchandise trade surplus hit a four-year high in May as exports reached a record C$77.1 billion. Gains were driven by metal ores and non-metallic minerals, while energy exports declined.

item.title: WTI Oil advances on Trump’s Iran shift, mounting Middle East supply risks
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil trades around $73.10 on Wednesday at the time of writing, up 1.48% on the day, as investors reassess risks to global energy supply following a renewed deterioration in geopolitical conditions across the Middle East.

item.title: Japanese Yen falls as renewed US-Iran tensions boost the US Dollar, Oil prices
item.description: USD/JPY edges higher on Wednesday as renewed escalation in the Middle East boosts demand for the US Dollar (USD) and lifts Oil prices, weighing on the Japanese Yen (JPY). At the time of writing, the pair is trading around 162.50, close to 40-year highs.

item.title: British Pound: Pound resilience faces political risks – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley highlights that the British Pound (GBP) has been a strong G10 performer this year, supported by sticky United Kingdom (UK) inflation, Bank of England (BoE) rate expectations and inbound M&A flows.

item.title: Euro: Political risks but downside bias – ING
item.description: Francesco Pesole at ING discusses Euro resilience despite French political developments, including Marine Le Pen’s 2027 bid and expectations of an RN win.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: RBNZ hawkish path supports currency – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports that the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) delivered a 25 bps hike to 2.50%, largely priced in, triggering an New Zealand Dollar (NZD) rally before gains were trimmed by Middle East tensions.

item.title: US Dollar: Warsh risks skewed to cuts – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Antje Praefcke argues that interest rate differentials are again driving the Dollar, with USD reacting strongly to weaker US data as markets reassess new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.

item.title: Oil: Conflict-driven volatility and positioning – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights growing fragility in global markets as President Trump declares the Iran ceasefire over and U.S. strikes in the Strait of Hormuz reignite Oil volatility.

item.title: Swiss Franc holds losses as fresh US-Iran tensions support the US Dollar
item.description: The Swiss Franc (CHF) nurses minor losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday but is depreciating nearly 0.7% so far this week.

item.title: British Pound slumps against US Dollar as risky assets turn fragile
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) is down 0.13% to near 1.3340 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Wednesday. The GBP/USD pair faces selling pressure as renewed geopolitical risks have diminished the appeal of riskier assets.

item.title: Polish Zloty: Dovish NBP stance weighs on PLN – ING
item.description: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky expects the National Bank of Poland (NBP) to keep rates at 3.75% through year-end, with easing delayed until policymakers gain confidence on inflation.
